### Observed differences

- Activity A02 disappeared while A01 appeared, in near mirror image: in the earlier window A02 ran in 92 of 200 traces (about 46 in 100) and A01 in none; in the later window A02 runs in none of 200 traces and A01 in 101 of 200 (about 50 in 100). Neither activity repeats within a trace in either window. [OCC001, OCC002]
- Both activities sit early in the trace when they occur: A02 at a median normalized position of about 0.11 in the earlier window, A01 at about 0.14 in the later window (means about 0.15 vs 0.19). [POS001, POS002]
- Each activity fans out to a similar, broad set of successors. Earlier, A02's outgoing transitions went most often to A03 (about 32%), A06 (about 22%) and A11 (about 14%); later, A01's go most often to A06 (about 24%), A03 (about 19%), and A10 and A11 (about 15% each). [DIR001, DIR002]
- The two activities never share a trace in either window: earlier, A02 appeared without A01 in about 46 in 100 traces (neither in 54); later, A01 appears without A02 in about 50 in 100 (neither in 50). [REL001]
- The swap propagates to neighbouring activities. Earlier, A02 co-occurred with A03 in 46 in 100 traces; later, A03 (present in every trace) always runs without A02, while A01 now co-occurs with A03 in about 50 in 100 traces in mixed order (A03 first about 20, interleaved about 26, A01 first about 5 in 100). A06 shows the same pattern: it co-occurred with A02 in about 26 in 100 traces earlier and now co-occurs with A01 in about 26 in 100. [REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that A01 took over the role previously played by A02. In the earlier window, A02 ran in about 46 in 100 cases, early in the trace, followed by a broad set of activities (most often A03, then A06 and A11). In the later window, A02 is never observed, and A01 runs in about 50 in 100 cases at a similar early position with a similar fan-out of successors (A06, A03, A10, A11, among others). The two activities never occur together, and their exclusive appearances exchange almost one-for-one between the windows. Supporting signs: the occurrence, direction, position and relation items all describe the same consistent picture, and 12 items qualified against roughly 0.21 expected if nothing had changed — far more than an unchanged process typically produces. Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish a genuinely new activity from a relabelling of the same step, and the successor mix is not identical (A02 favoured A03 at about 32%, whereas A01 favours A06 at about 24%), so the routing out of this early step may also have shifted somewhat; most items describe one underlying swap and are not independent confirmations.

Other differences: A03's own outgoing transitions were slightly redistributed (cosine dissimilarity about 0.05): A01 now receives about 8% of A03's outgoing transitions where A02 previously received about 7%, and A10's share rose from about 32% to about 37%. [DIR003]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Setup:
- 200 traces before, 200 traces after.
- Screening: 43 units tested, 12 items qualified, 0.21 expected by chance (control_flow family only). 12 items is many times larger than 0.21 — so the count of evidence items cannot be explained by chance as a whole. So we move past the "insufficient evidence by count" gate.

Evidence items (12 total):
1. OCC001: A01 — before: 0 participation, after: 0.505 participation (about 101 of 200 traces). Mean occurrences per trace 0.505, recurrence support 0 (so A01 occurs at most once per trace). A01 appeared in the later window in about half the traces, absent before.
2. OCC002: A02 — before: 0.46 participation (92 of 200), after: 0. A02 disappeared.
3. DIR001: A01 outgoing transitions — before empty (A01 never observed), after: transitions to A05 (0.079), A03 (0.188), A06 (0.238), A13 (0.109), A10 (0.149), A09 (0.020), A11 (0.149), A04 (0.069). So A01, when it occurs, is followed by various activities.
4. DIR002: A02 outgoing — before: transitions to A03 (0.315), A06 (0.217), A11 (0.141), A13 (0.109), A04 (0.087), A10 (0.065), A05 (0.033), A09 (0.022), A08 (0.011); after: empty. A02 gone.
5. DIR003: A03 outgoing — before vs after: A01 appears as a successor (0.081) after; A02 disappears as successor (was 0.067). Slight redistribution, observed_change 0.046.
6. POS001: A01 position — after: mean position ~0.185 (normalized), median ~0.14, q75 ~0.29. Before: no support. So A01 occurs early in traces.
7. POS002: A02 position — before: mean ~0.145, median ~0.105; after: gone.
8. REL001: A01–A02 — before: B_only (A02 only) 0.46, neither 0.54; after: A_only (A01 only) 0.505, neither 0.495. So A01 and A02 never co-occur; before A02 appeared alone in 46% of traces, after A01 appears alone in ~50%.
9. REL002: A01–A03 — before: B_only (A03 only) 1.0 (A03 in all traces, A01 never); after: cooccurrence 0.505, B_only 0.495, with order mixed: A_before_B 0.05, B_before_A 0.2, interleaved 0.255. So A01 now co-occurs with A03 in about half the traces, in mixed order.
10. REL003: A01–A06 — before: B_only 0.53, neither 0.47; after: cooccurrence 0.255, A_only 0.25, B_only 0.245, neither 0.25, mixed orders. So A01 and A06 now sometimes co-occur.
11. REL004: A02–A03 — before: cooccurrence 0.46, B_only 0.54, with mixed order (A_before_B 0.12, B_before_A 0.165, interleaved 0.175); after: B_only 1.0. So A02 used to co-occur with A03 in 46% of traces; now A03 always occurs without A02.
12. REL005: A02–A06 — before: cooccurrence 0.26, A_only 0.2, B_only 0.27, neither 0.27; after: B_only 0.5, neither 0.5. So A02 gone.

Interpretation: A02 was present in ~46% of traces before (occurring early, mean position ~0.145), with outgoing transitions to many activities (A03 most common at ~32% of A02's outgoing transitions). After the change point, A02 is completely absent, and A01 appears in ~50% of traces, early (median position ~0.14), with outgoing transitions to a similar set of activities (A03 ~19%, A06 ~24%, A10 ~15%, A11 ~15%, A13 ~11%, A05 ~8%, A04 ~7%, A09 ~2%).

This looks like a replacement of one activity by another: A02 replaced by A01. The outgoing transition profiles are similar but not identical: A02's biggest successor was A03 (0.315), A01's biggest is A06 (0.238) then A03 (0.188), A10 (0.149), A11 (0.149). Both have broad fan-out to the same set of activities (A03, A04, A05, A06, A09, A10, A11, A13; A02 also had A08 slightly).

REL001 shows A01 and A02 never co-occur: before A02_only 0.46, after A01_only 0.505. This is consistent with a one-for-one replacement — they behave like alternatives, or rather like the same role occupied by different activities in the two windows.

REL002: A03 occurs in all traces both windows. Before, A03 never co-occurred with A01 (A01 absent); after, co-occurs in ~50%. REL004: before A02 co-occurred with A03 in 46%; after A03 always without A02.

So the hypothesis: activity A02 was replaced by A01 — A01 took over the role A02 had. A01 appears in about half the traces in the later window (101/200), at a similar early position (median ~0.14 vs ~0.11 for A02), and leads to a similar set of successor activities. A02 disappeared entirely.

Is this "replacement" or "A02 removed and A01 added"? The evidence supports: A02 no longer occurs; A01 now occurs in about half the traces, early, with a broad set of successors similar to A02's. The participation rates: A02 46% before, A01 50.5% after — similar. Positions similar. Successor sets overlap heavily (A03, A04, A05, A06, A09, A10, A11, A13; A02 additionally A08 at 1%).

This is a direct, consistent story across OCC, DIR, POS, REL items. 12 items vs 0.21 expected — many times larger. So we're past the screening gate.

Support level: The hypothesis "A01 replaced A02" — is it directly supported? The evidence shows:
- A02 present before (46% of traces), absent after (0/200).
- A01 absent before (0/200), present after (101/200, ~50%).
- Similar early positions.
- Similar successor distributions (both fan out to the same set of activities).
- Never co-occur (REL001).

This is a structural change: an activity swap/replacement. The relational evidence (REL001) directly shows they are mutually exclusive and their participations swapped. DIR evidence shows similar successor profiles. POS shows similar positions.

Competing explanations: Could it be that A02 was renamed to A01 (same behaviour, different label)? That's essentially the replacement hypothesis. Could A01 be a new activity inserted at a similar point while A02 was removed for a different reason? The evidence can't distinguish "same activity relabelled" from "different activity taking over the role". Also, the successor distributions differ somewhat (A02 favoured A03 at 32%; A01 favours A06 at 24% and A03 at 19%), so the downstream routing isn't identical — but that could be sampling or a genuine difference.

Also DIR003: A03's outgoing transitions changed slightly — A01 now appears as a successor of A03 (8% of A03's outgoing), A02 no longer (was 6.7%). This is consistent: A03 now sometimes followed by A01 (REL002 shows B_before_A 0.2 — A03 before A01 in 20% of traces, interleaved 0.255). Hmm, wait — DIR003 shows A01 as a successor of A03 in the after window. And REL002 shows mixed order between A01 and A03. Consistent.

Is this a "change in how often existing paths are taken"? No — A01 was absent before and A02 is absent after, so it's an addition/removal/replacement, not a path-frequency shift. The instructions say: "A change in how often existing paths are taken requires that every activity and path involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows... It does not apply when an activity or path is (nearly) absent in one window." So we should not frame it as path-frequency shift; it's activity replacement (one activity removed, another added taking a similar role).

Hypothesis level: Supported hypothesis? The evidence directly and consistently shows: A02 disappeared, A01 appeared, similar participation, similar position, similar successors, mutually exclusive. That's direct evidence for a replacement-type change. The main limitation: we cannot tell whether A01 is the same underlying step relabelled or a genuinely different activity taking over the role; and the successor mix differs somewhat (A02 → A03 was the top successor at ~32%, whereas A01 → A06 is top at ~24% with A03 at ~19%).

I think "Supported hypothesis" is appropriate: the change (A02 out, A01 in, at a similar early position with a similar fan-out of successors) is shown directly by occurrence, direction, position and relation items that all agree. The screening count (12 vs 0.21 expected) confirms this isn't chance-level noise.

Alternatively "Weak hypothesis"? The guidance: Supported = "the evidence supports a specific hypothesis directly and consistently". Here we have direct evidence: OCC shows presence/absence swap; REL001 directly shows the swap pattern (B_only → A_only, never co-occurring); DIR shows successor profiles; POS shows similar positions. Consistent across 12 items. I'd say Supported hypothesis, with the limitation that relabelling vs. genuine new activity can't be distinguished, and the successor mix shifted somewhat.

Main hypothesis: A01 took over the role previously played by A02: before, A02 ran in about 46 in 100 cases early in the trace (median normalized position ~0.11) and was followed by a spread of activities (most often A03, ~32% of its outgoing transitions); after, A02 never appears, and A01 runs in about 50 in 100 cases at a similar early position (median ~0.14), followed by a similar spread (A06 ~24%, A03 ~19%, A10 and A11 ~15% each). The two never occur in the same case (REL001).

Other differences: DIR003 — A03's outgoing mix shifted slightly: A01 now appears as a successor (~8% of A03's outgoing transitions) while A02 no longer does (was ~7%); A10's share rose from ~32% to ~37%. This is largely a consequence of the main swap. REL002/REL003: A01 now co-occurs with A03 (in ~50% of cases) and with A06 (in ~26% of cases) in mixed orders — consequences of A01's arrival. REL004/REL005: A03 and A06 no longer co-occur with A02 — consequences of A02's departure.

I should be careful: "Several indicators and activities can reflect the same trace behaviour; agreeing items are not automatically independent confirmations." So I should note the items largely describe one underlying swap.

Numbers to use:
- A02: 92 of 200 traces before (46%), 0 of 200 after.
- A01: 0 of 200 before, 101 of 200 after (~50%).
- Positions: A02 median normalized position ~0.11 before; A01 median ~0.14 after (both early, within roughly the first third of the trace). Mean 0.145 vs 0.185.
- Successors: A02 before: A03 ~32%, A06 ~22%, A11 ~14%, A13 ~11%, A04 ~9%, A10 ~7%, A05 ~3%, A09 ~2%, A08 ~1% (shares of A02's outgoing transitions, 92 traces). A01 after: A06 ~24%, A03 ~19%, A10 ~15%, A11 ~15%, A13 ~11%, A05 ~8%, A04 ~7%, A09 ~2% (101 traces).
- REL001: before A02 without A01 in 46% of traces, neither 54%; after A01 without A02 in ~50%, neither ~50%. Never co-occur in either window.
- REL004: before A02 and A03 together in 46% of traces; after A03 always without A02 (100% B_only).
- REL002: after A01 and A03 together in ~50% of traces, in mixed order (A03 first ~20%, A01 first ~5%, interleaved/repeated ~26%).
- REL003: after A01 and A06 together in ~26% of traces.

Screening: 12 items qualified vs 0.21 expected without change — many times larger, so chance cannot explain the set.

Every factual bullet must end with exactly one [id list]. Let me draft.

### Observed differences

- Activity A02 ran in about 46 in 100 cases in the earlier window (92 of 200 traces) and in none of the 200 later-window traces; activity A01 shows the mirror image, absent earlier and present in about 50 in 100 later cases (101 of 200). Neither activity repeats within a trace. [OCC001, OCC002]

- When present, each activity fans out to a similar, broad set of successors. Earlier, A02's outgoing transitions went most often to A03 (about 32%), A06 (about 22%) and A11 (about 14%). Later, A01's go most often to A06 (about 24%), A03 (about 19%), and A10/A11 (about 15% each). [DIR001, DIR002]

Screening note: 12 items qualified against 0.21 expected by chance — I can mention in inference.

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

Main hypothesis: A01 took over the role previously played by A02. Before, A02 ran in roughly 46 in 100 cases, early in the trace, followed by a broad set of activities (most often A03); after, A02 is never observed and A01 runs in roughly 50 in 100 cases at a similar early position with a similar fan-out of successors (A06, A03, A10, A11 among others). The two never appear together, and their arrival/departure mirrors each other almost one-for-one. Supporting signs: occurrence, direction, position and relation items all agree; 12 qualifying items versus about 0.21 expected by chance.

Limitations / competing explanation: the evidence cannot distinguish a genuine replacement of A02 by a new activity A01 from a relabelling of the same step; and the successor mix is not identical (A02 favoured A03 at ~32%, A01 favours A06 at ~24%), so the downstream routing may also have shifted somewhat. Also, most items describe the same underlying swap, so they are not independent confirmations.

Other differences: DIR003's small redistribution at A03 (A10 share up, A01 in / A02 out) — largely a by-product of the swap.

Hmm — should the "Other differences" be separate? The DIR003 shift is arguably part of the main hypothesis (A03's successors changed because A02→A01). One caution: "POS and LAG use event positions, not clock time. A position shift alone does not show that an activity was moved." I'm using position only to say both occur early — descriptive, fine.

Support level decision: The hypothesis "A01 replaced A02 in the same early role" is directly supported by occurrence (mirror-image presence/absence), relation (never co-occur, swapped exclusive appearance), position (both early), and direction (similar successor sets). This is direct and consistent. I'll go with Supported hypothesis, noting the relabel-vs-new-activity limitation and the somewhat shifted successor mix.

Actually, let me reconsider whether "Supported" vs "Weak" is right. The core claim: A02 was removed and A01 added, occupying a similar role. Chance sampling — ruled out by the screening count and the complete absence/presence (0/200 and 101/200 are not sampling fluctuations of a stable process at these rates... well, an activity at 46% participation dropping to 0 in 200 traces is essentially impossible by chance; empirical strength 0.995 supports). Another competitor: A01 inserted as a new parallel optional step while A02 removed for unrelated reasons — but the similarity in position and successors and the exclusive pattern make the takeover reading the most direct. I think Supported is defensible, with limitations stated.
